history.origins: Treikort was played widely in Iceland up to the last century. Old Danish games manuals describe a different game also called Treikort; the Icelandic form is distinct. It is sometimes called "3-man Alkort". The game is documented in Ólafur Davíðsson's writings on Icelandic amusements (1887–1903, Copenhagen) and in Spilabók AB by Þ. Guðmundsson (1989, Reykjavík).
timeline: 19th–20th century: Played widely in Iceland; described in Spilabók AB (Þ. Guðmundsson, 1989) and in Ólafur Davíðsson's writings on Icelandic amusements (1887–1903).

setup.dealing: Deal 9 cards each (3 at a time).

rules.objective: The object of the game is to take as many tricks as possible (nine tricks per deal).
rules.gameplay: Lead a card. Must follow suit if possible. Highest card wins (no trumps). Sevens: Unbeatable when LED, cannot win if played to follow. Cannot lead a 7 until you've won a trick. Ties: First played wins.
